dossier.scp_unleashed.149.title: Blood Flies
dossier.scp_unleashed.149.caption: SCP-149 in a feeding enclosure shortly after a meal, abdomen swollen. A cocoon rests on the floor behind it.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-149 instances are to be kept together in a sealed enclosure of reinforced glass, set inside a second, larger cell with no other openings.
**Exposed skin is not permitted anywhere in the containment wing.**
Instances are to be fed live animals through the feeding hatch on a fixed schedule. The schedule is not to slip. %rInterval withheld.%r
Any person bitten is to be isolated at once and watched until cleared. Red cocoons found anywhere on site are to be reported immediately %rand destroyed%r.

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-149 is a species of mosquito-like insect of unusual size. Adult instances are nearly a metre long, with a dark, glossy head and thorax, six long banded legs, a straight proboscis and a long abdomen that turns a deep red once the instance has fed.

SCP-149 flies quickly and unpredictably. It closes on a target in short darts, bites, and pulls away before it can be struck, then returns. Instances seek out people above all other prey, but will feed on any animal within reach.

A person bitten by SCP-149 becomes SCP-149-1. At first nothing is noticed. Within minutes the subject begins to tremble and reports movement under the skin; moments later the whole brood of small red larvae bursts out of them at once. %rThe subject's condition is not described further in this file.%r

The larvae avoid people and wander for a while before seeking each other out. Where enough of them meet, they spin a red cocoon. The cocoon darkens and pulses as it grows, and in time it splits open. One adult emerges for every larva sealed inside.

Instances that go hungry grow agitated and try to leave their enclosure, chewing through whatever stands in the way. The weakest part of an enclosure goes first. Instances kept together appear to share their hunger.

page.title: Addendum 149-1: Appearance
page.text: SCP-149 has no recovery site. Readers of this file have reported a high, thin whine some time afterwards, followed by a single instance, close by and in plain view.

page.title: Addendum 149-2: Population
page.text: However many hosts have been available, the number of living adults has never exceeded a certain figure. %rThe figure is withheld.%r Cocoons formed past that point did not open fully. Whatever was left inside waited.

page.title: Addendum 149-3: Field Note
page.text: You hear the whine before you see it. By then it has already picked you. Keep covered, keep moving, and do not let anything small and red crawl away.

message.scp_unleashed.scp149.itch.0: Something whines close to your ear.
message.scp_unleashed.scp149.itch.2: You keep hearing wings that are not there.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp149_fly_spawn_: SCP-149, a blood fly: a mosquito-like insect nearly a metre long, with a dark head and thorax, a long red abdomen and a straight, needle-like proboscis. It has %s health.
It flies fast and erratically, darts in to bite and pulls away before it can be struck, then comes back. It goes for people first, but it will feed on any living thing it can reach.
People it bites are not left alone for long. Instances kept together seem to share their hunger.
It does not occur naturally; its archive file has more on where it comes from. Hungry instances do not stay where they are put.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp149_larva_spaw: An SCP-149 larva: a small, bright red, segmented grub. Larvae come out of people who have been bitten.
They are harmless on their own and keep away from people. After crawling about for a while, they go looking for each other.
Whatever they build together should not be left alone.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp149_cocoon.1: SCP-149 cocoon: a red casing spun by gathered SCP-149 larvae.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp149_cocoon.2: It slowly grows, darkens and beats faster as it matures. In time it splits open.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp149_cocoon.3: It is soft and tears easily.
